16: 17: --- 18: 19: ## 📋 Table of Contents 20: 21: - [The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation](#-the-vision-context-aware-innovation) 22: - [Current State (Experimental Testbed)](#-current-state-experimental-testbed) 23: - [Code Overview](#-code-overview) 24: - [Getting Started](#-getting-started) 25: - [Command-Line Interface (CLI)](#-command-line-interface-cli) 26: - [Interactive Chat](#-interactive-chat) 27: - [Manage Customer Outcomes](#-manage-customer-outcomes) 28: - [External Connectors (MCP, REST, Webhook)](#-external-connectors-mcp-rest-webhook) 29: - [Living Studio Run Modes](#-living-studio-run-modes) 30: - [Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend](#-local-tools-capable-llm-backend-for-mcp-testing) 31: - [Agent-Driven Testing](#-agent-driven-testing) 32: - [Linting, Formatting & Type Checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) 33: - [Testing](#-testing) 34: - [Test Coverage Map](#-test-coverage-map) 35: - [Agent Session Tracking](#-agent-session-tracking) 36: - [Superpowers with Pi](#-superpowers-with-pi) 37: - [Developer Workflow for Formatting](#-developer-workflow-for-formatting) 38: - [Superpowers with Freebuff](#-superpowers-with-freebuff) 39: - [Deployment](#-deployment) 40: - [Roadmap & Next Steps](#-roadmap--next-steps) 41: - [Contributing](#-contributing) 42: - [License](#-license) 43: 44: --- 45: 46: ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation 47: 48: **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. 49: 50: **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 51: 52: The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. 53: 54: --- 55: 56: ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) 57: 58: This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. 59: 60: --- 61: 62: ## 🧩 Code Overview 63: 64: This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of **six** installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own build, tests, and layout: 65: 66: | Package | Description | 67: |---|---| 68: | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models (Jobs, Steps, desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, and Evidence), the `ODIService` business-logic layer, JSON schema export, outcome-statement evaluation, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite) with ODI opportunity-score computation. | 69: | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | An MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, schema discovery, and `evaluate_outcome`. | 70: | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | The FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. It talks to the MCP server on the client's behalf and serves the Studio API — configuration, health probes, canvas data, MCP mutations, and streaming (SSE) chat with the LLM tool-loop — plus the built SPA when `studio/dist` exists. | 71: | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | The local dev **launcher** (`run.py` / `python -m client.run`) that starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together. (Its former Streamlit UI has been replaced by the `studio/` SPA.) | 72: | **`studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`studio/src-tauri/`). | 73: | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode, `version`/`update`, and full CRUD for `jobs`, `steps`, `outcomes`, `customer-outcomes`, and `evidence`, plus top-level `score` and `schema` commands. | 74: | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations: **MCP client**, **REST**, and **webhook** connectors implementing one `Connector` protocol. Connector records are normalized into `IngestBatch`es; a separate mapping module turns them into ODI evidence drafts without coupling connector plumbing to the store. | 75: 76: --- 77: 78: ## 🚀 Getting Started 79: 80: ### Prerequisites 81: 82: - **Python** 3.10+ 83: - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager 84: 85: Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling): 86: 87: ```bash 88: uv sync --all-packages 89: ``` 90: 91: This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode. 92: 93: ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) 94: 95: The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal. It provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. 96: 97: Launch it with: 98: 99: ```bash 100: python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version 101: python -m cli --help # show available options and commands 102: python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped) 103: ``` 104: 105: A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. 106: 107: **Vocabulary:** `outcomes` means *desired Outcomes* (the ODI center of gravity). Customer Outcomes — the link between customer value and business value — live under `customer-outcomes`. 108: 109: **Global options:** 110: 111: | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning | 112: |---|---|---|---| 113: | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Read/write directly through SQLite, or call the running MCP server. | 114: | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. `:memory:` makes it ephemeral. | 115: | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | MCP server URL for the `mcp` backend. | 116: 117: ```bash 118: # Jobs 119: agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard customers" --description "Reduce time to first value" 120: agentic-odi jobs list 121: agentic-odi jobs get 122: agentic-odi jobs update --name "Onboard new customers" 123: agentic-odi jobs delete --yes 124: 125: # Job-map steps 126: agentic-odi steps add --job-id --name "Sign up" --order 1 127: agentic-odi steps list --job-id 128: agentic-odi steps update --order 2 129: 130: # Desired outcomes (score is computed as importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)) 131: agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --statement "Minimize the time to resolve setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 132: agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id 133: agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 134: 135: # Top-level helpers 136: agentic-odi score 8 2 # 14.00 137: agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity 138: ``` 139: 140: ### 💬 Interactive Chat 141: 142: `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts a conversational session against the MCP server and an OpenAI-compatible LLM. Responses stream to the terminal, and the assistant can call the ODI MCP tools as it talks. 143: 144: ```bash 145: agentic-odi chat 146: agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp 147: ``` 148: 149: Before starting, run the MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`) and point the chat at an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint. The chat reads the same environment variables as the Living Studio: 150: 151: | Variable | Default | CLI flag | 152: |---|---|---| 153: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` | 154: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` | 155: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` | 156: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` | 157: 158: Inside the session, `/help` lists the commands, `/tools` lists the MCP tools the assistant can call, `/clear` resets the conversation, and `/exit` (or `/quit`) ends the session. 159: 160: > [!NOTE] 161: > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `outcomes` and `connectors` commands keep working without one. 162: 163: ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes 164: 165: Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The `local` backend writes to the shared SQLite store by default; add `--backend mcp` to route through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`): 166: 167: ```bash 168: # Add a Customer Outcome (repeat --value-metric for nested metrics) 169: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" --value-metric '{"name":"setup errors","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"count","importance":9,"satisfaction":3}' 170: 171: # List outcomes (optionally filtered) 172: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list 173: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id 174: 175: # Get, update, delete 176: agentic-odi customer-outcomes get 177: agentic-odi customer-outcomes update --importance 9.0 178: agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete --yes 179: ``` 180: 181: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server if needed. 182: 183: ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP, REST, Webhook) 184: 185: Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). Every kind implements the same `Connector` protocol and normalizes payloads into `IngestBatch` records. 186: 187: ```bash 188: # MCP: act as an MCP client and pull catalog, resources, and configured tools 189: python -m cli connectors add mcp --name gong --url http://localhost:9000/mcp --tool latest_quote 190: 191: # REST: pull a JSON document and read records from a dot path 192: python -m cli connectors add rest --name jira --url https://jira.example/api/issues --header "Authorization=Bearer $TOKEN" --records-key result.issues 193: 194: # Webhook: POST a configured request to a webhook inbox and ingest its response 195: python -m cli connectors add webhook --name feedback --url https://hooks.example/inbox --method POST 196: 197: python -m cli connectors list 198: python -m cli connectors health --name gong 199: python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong 200: ``` 201: 202: Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and appended to the in-process ingest sink. Pass `--job-id`, `--step-id`, or `--outcome-id` to also map evidence-bearing records into the ODI store, then promote them when they are ready: 203: 204: ```bash 205: python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong --job-id 206: agentic-odi evidence list --job-id 207: agentic-odi evidence promote --to outcome --job-id --statement "Minimize the time to onboard when signing up" --importance 8 --satisfaction 4 208: ``` 209: 210: Mapping stays separate from the connector package: connectors emit records, `connectors.mapping` produces evidence drafts, and the CLI writes them to the ODI store. 211: 212: ### ⚡ Living Studio Run Modes 213: 214: The Living Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly. 215: 216: **Architecture** 217: 218: ```text 219: ┌────────────────────────────┐ /api (JSON) ┌───────────────────────────────┐ 220: │ Living Studio SPA │ ────────────▶ │ local_server (sidecar) │ 221: │ React + TS + Vite │ /api/chat │ FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100 │ 222: │ (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │ - config / health / canvas │ 223: └────────────────────────────┘ SSE stream │ - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │ 224: │ - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop) │ 225: └───────────────┬───────────────┘ 226: │ MCP (HTTP) 227: ▼ 228: ┌───────────────────────────────┐ 229: │ mcp_server :8000/mcp │ 230: └───────────────────────────────┘ 231: ▲ 232: │ OpenAI-compatible 233: ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐ 234: │ Your local LLM backend │ 235: └───────────────────────────────┘ 236: ``` 237: 238: **1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)** 239: 240: ```bash 241: npm --prefix studio run build # build the SPA into studio/dist 242: python -m client.run # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100 243: ``` 244: 245: | Service | URL | 246: |---|---| 247: | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | 248: | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | 249: 250: **2. Web — dev with hot reload** (Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar): 251: 252: ```bash 253: npm --prefix studio run dev:full # MCP + sidecar + Vite together 254: # open http://localhost:5173 255: ``` 256: 257: **3. Desktop — Tauri 2** (the app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself): 258: 259: ```bash 260: npm --prefix studio run tauri dev # dev window 261: npm --prefix studio run tauri build # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows) 262: ``` 263: 264: > [!NOTE] 265: > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu: 266: > 267: > ```bash 268: > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \ 269: > libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64 270: > ``` 271: > 272: > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`. 273: 274: #### 🔐 Desktop signing & updater secrets 275: 276: Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub Actions secrets. 277: 278: | Secret | Purpose | 279: |---|---| 280: | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. | 281: | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). | 282: | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. | 283: | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. | 284: | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. | 285: | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. | 286: 287: Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via **Settings → Check for updates**. 288: 289: #### 🔑 Managing the updater signing key 290: 291: The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in CI, or attached to a build artifact. 292: 293: 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it: 294: 295: ```bash 296: npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f 297: ``` 298: 299: This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub` (public). 300: 301: 2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`: 302: 303: ```jsonc 304: { 305: "plugins": { 306: "updater": { 307: "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"], 308: "pubkey": "" 309: } 310: } 311: } 312: ``` 313: 314: 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions: 315: 316: ```bash 317: mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys 318: mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/ 319: chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key 320: ``` 321: 322: Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives. Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing installs. 323: 324: 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI: 325: 326: ```bash 327: gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key 328: gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body "" # only if you set a password 329: ``` 330: 331: 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed): 332: 333: ```bash 334: gh secret list 335: ``` 336: 337: 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public key ahead of the cut-over. 338: 339: > [!CAUTION] 340: > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release. 341: 342: > [!IMPORTANT] 343: > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI formulas are unchanged. 344: 345: ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) 346: 347: To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: 348: 349: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and 350: - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. 351: 352: A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 353: 354: 1. **Install a local LLM server** 355: 356: Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): 357: 358: ```bash 359: pip install llama-cpp-python 360: ``` 361: 362: 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** 363: 364: Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 365: 366: 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** 367: 368: Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Living Studio sidecar: 369: 370: ```bash 371: python -m llama_cpp.server \ 372: --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ 373: --model_alias local-tools-model \ 374: --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ 375: --chat_format openai 376: ``` 377: 378: This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 379: 380: 4. **Point the Living Studio at the local server** 381: 382: The sidecar reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks): 383: 384: | Variable | Default | 385: |---|---| 386: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | 387: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | 388: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | 389: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | 390: 391: You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's **Settings** panel. 392: 393: 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** 394: 395: - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: 396: 397: ```bash 398: curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models 399: ``` 400: 401: If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. 402: 403: - Start the MCP server and the Living Studio (via `python -m client.run` or `npm --prefix studio run dev:full`). 404: - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.” 405: - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. 406: - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. 407: 408: ### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing 409: 410: Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. 411: 412: --- 413: 414: ## 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) 415: 416: The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: 417: 418: ```bash 419: # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) 420: uv run ruff check . 421: uv run ruff format --check . 422: 423: # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) 424: uv run --directory core mypy . 425: uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . 426: uv run --directory local_server mypy . 427: uv run --directory client mypy . 428: uv run --directory cli mypy . 429: uv run --directory connectors mypy . 430: 431: # Security scanning 432: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src 433: 434: # Tests (same as CI) 435: uv run --directory core pytest 436: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest 437: uv run --directory local_server pytest 438: uv run --directory client pytest 439: uv run --directory cli pytest 440: uv run --directory connectors pytest 441: ``` 442: 443: ### 🖥️ Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio) 444: 445: The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally: 446: 447: ```bash 448: npm --prefix studio run lint # ESLint 449: npm --prefix studio run typecheck # tsc --noEmit 450: npm --prefix studio test -- --run # Vitest (run once) 451: npm --prefix studio run build # production build → studio/dist 452: cd studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check 453: ``` 454: 455: To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: 456: 457: ```bash 458: uv tool install pre-commit 459: pre-commit install 460: ``` 461: 462: After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: 463: 464: ```bash 465: pre-commit run --all-files 466: ``` 467: 468: --- 469: 470: ## ✅ Testing 471: 472: Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: 473: 474: ```bash 475: uv run --directory core pytest 476: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest 477: uv run --directory local_server pytest 478: uv run --directory client pytest 479: uv run --directory cli pytest 480: uv run --directory connectors pytest 481: ``` 482: 483: ### 📊 Test Coverage Map 484: 485: | File | What it covers | 486: |---|---| 487: | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | 488: | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` entity CRUD, FK validation, evidence promotion, score recompute | 489: | `core/tests/test_repository.py` | In-memory repository CRUD and cascade deletes (including evidence) | 490: | `core/tests/test_sqlite_repository.py` | Read-through SQLite persistence, cascade replay, evidence round-trips | 491: | `core/tests/test_schema.py` | Canonical JSON schema export for every ODI entity | 492: | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | 493: | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | 494: | `mcp_server/tests/test_context_tools.py` | `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_schema`, and Evidence MCP tools | 495: | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | 496: | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | 497: | `mcp_server/tests/test_parity.py` | Job/Step/Outcome CRUD tool parity and `value_metrics` updates | 498: | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | 499: | `local_server/tests/test_studio_api.py` | Living Studio sidecar API (config, health, canvas, SSE chat, steps/outcomes) | 500: | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks, mcp + sidecar commands) | 501: | `studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client | 502: | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | 503: | `cli/tests/test_backend.py` | Backend abstraction and full local tool dispatch | 504: | `cli/tests/test_backend_selection.py` | `--backend` selection routes to local or MCP | 505: | `cli/tests/test_jobs_cli.py` | Jobs CLI CRUD and backend selection | 506: | `cli/tests/test_steps_cli.py` | Job-map Steps CLI | 507: | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Desired Outcomes CLI and top-level `score` | 508: | `cli/tests/test_customer_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI with `--value-metric` JSON | 509: | `cli/tests/test_evidence_cli.py` | Evidence capture, filtering, delete, and promotion | 510: | `cli/tests/test_persistence.py` | Every entity type survives a fresh repository | 511: | `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | `connectors` add/list/health/ingest and evidence mapping | 512: | `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON connector registry persist/load and kind checks | 513: | `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | In-memory FastMCP health and ingest records | 514: | `connectors/tests/test_rest_connector.py` | REST/webhook health and record normalization with a fake transport | 515: | `connectors/tests/test_mapping.py` | Connector records → evidence drafts (catalog filtering, links) | 516: 517: **Conventions:** 518: 519: - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. 520: - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. 521: - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. 522: - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. 523: 524: > [!TIP] 525: > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. 526: 527: ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking 528: 529: Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. 530: 531: --- 532: 533: ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi 534: 535: This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). Freebuff discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool. 571: - **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules, the Freebuff tool mapping, and the mandatory one-worktree-per-task rule at session start. 572: - **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` maps skill actions to Freebuff tools. 573: 574: Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify. See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for update and troubleshooting notes. 575: 576: --- 577: 578: ## Quick Install (Binary) 579: 580: Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install the latest release with one command: 581: 582: ```bash 583: curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh 584: ``` 585: 586: The installer places the binary under `~/.local/share/agentic-odi/versions//`, creates a `current` symlink, and symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. 587: 588: If `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH, add it (e.g., `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`). On Windows, the PowerShell installer uses `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\` and copies `.exe` files to `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\bin\`. 589: 590: ### Update 591: 592: By default, `odi` auto-checks for updates once every 24 hours and applies the update on the next run (auto-update is enabled by default). Control behavior with: 593: 594: - `odi update` — explicit check and update 595: - `--no-update` flag — skip auto-update for this run 596: - `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` — disable auto-update globally 597: 598: When running from a non-frozen source install, auto-update is suppressed automatically. 599: 600: ### Install layout 601: 602: ``` 603: ~/.local/share/agentic-odi/ 604: ├── versions// 605: │ └── odi (and bundled files) 606: └── current -> versions/ 607: 608: ~/.local/bin/ 609: ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi 610: ├── odipm 611: ├── odi-cli 612: └── agentic-odi 613: 614: ~/.config/agentic-odi/ # state/preferences 615: ``` 616: 617: Environment variables: `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR` (override install root), `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_BIN_HOME`. The default backend is `local` (`--backend local`); no MCP server is required. 618: 619: ### Unsigned binaries 620: 621: macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi` (if needed). Windows SmartScreen may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you trust the release. 622: 623: ## ☁️ Deployment 624: 625: The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. 626: 627: ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) 628: 629: Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: 630: 631: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** 632: 633: ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint 634: 635: Integrate via the MCP protocol at: 636: 637: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** 638: 639: > [!IMPORTANT] 640: > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client. 641: 642: --- 643: 644: ## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps 645: 646: All roadmap milestones below are implemented: 647: 648: - [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests. 649: - [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: `connectors.mapping` turns ingest records into evidence drafts; `connectors ingest --job-id/--step-id/--outcome-id` captures evidence, and `evidence promote` turns a record into a Job or desired Outcome without coupling connector plumbing to the ODI store. 650: - [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST and webhook connectors implement the same `Connector` protocol, with injectable HTTP transports for tests. 651: - [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Pydantic models for Jobs, Steps, Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, and Evidence, plus `core.odi_schema()` / `agentic-odi schema` / `get_odi_schema` for the canonical JSON Schema. 652: - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: `jobs`, `steps`, `outcomes`, `customer-outcomes`, `evidence`, `score`, and `schema` work against the local SQLite store or the MCP backend. 653: - [x] **Context Tooling**: `get_job_map(job_id)`, `evaluate_outcome(statement)`, `get_odi_schema()`, and the Evidence tools replace the dummy `greet` tool. 654: - [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: The FastMCP server and CLI share a read-through SQLite repository (WAL + append-only event log) at `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`. 655: - [x] **Agentic Integration**: The Living Studio and CLI chat connect an OpenAI-compatible LLM to the MCP server, discover tools with `list_tools`, and let the model call them while ideating features. 656: 657: --- 658: 659: ## 🤝 Contributing 660: 661: Contributions are welcome! Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of **six** installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own build, tests, and layout: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models (Jobs, Steps, desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, and Evidence), the `ODIService` business-logic layer, JSON schema export, outcome-statement evaluation, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite) with ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | An MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, schema discovery, and `evaluate_outcome`. | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | The FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. It talks to the MCP server on the client's behalf and serves the Studio API — configuration, health probes, canvas data, MCP mutations, and streaming (SSE) chat with the LLM tool-loop — plus the built SPA when `studio/dist` exists. | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | The local dev **launcher** (`run.py` / `python -m client.run`) that starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together. (Its former Streamlit UI has been replaced by the `studio/` SPA.) | | **`studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`studio/src-tauri/`). | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode, `version`/`update`, and full CRUD for `jobs`, `steps`, `outcomes`, `customer-outcomes`, and `evidence`, plus top-level `score` and `schema` commands. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations: **MCP client**, **REST**, and **webhook** connectors implementing one `Connector` protocol. Connector records are normalized into `IngestBatch`es; a separate mapping module turns them into ODI evidence drafts without coupling connector plumbing to the store. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode. ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal. It provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Launch it with: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped) ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. **Vocabulary:** `outcomes` means *desired Outcomes* (the ODI center of gravity). Customer Outcomes — the link between customer value and business value — live under `customer-outcomes`. **Global options:** | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Read/write directly through SQLite, or call the running MCP server. | | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. `:memory:` makes it ephemeral. | | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | MCP server URL for the `mcp` backend. | ```bash # Jobs agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard customers" --description "Reduce time to first value" agentic-odi jobs list agentic-odi jobs get agentic-odi jobs update --name "Onboard new customers" agentic-odi jobs delete --yes # Job-map steps agentic-odi steps add --job-id --name "Sign up" --order 1 agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi steps update --order 2 # Desired outcomes (score is computed as importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)) agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --statement "Minimize the time to resolve setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 # Top-level helpers agentic-odi score 8 2 # 14.00 agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity ``` ### 💬 Interactive Chat `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts a conversational session against the MCP server and an OpenAI-compatible LLM. Responses stream to the terminal, and the assistant can call the ODI MCP tools as it talks. ```bash agentic-odi chat agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp ``` Before starting, run the MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`) and point the chat at an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint. The chat reads the same environment variables as the Living Studio: | Variable | Default | CLI flag | |---|---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` | Inside the session, `/help` lists the commands, `/tools` lists the MCP tools the assistant can call, `/clear` resets the conversation, and `/exit` (or `/quit`) ends the session. > [!NOTE] > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `outcomes` and `connectors` commands keep working without one. ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The `local` backend writes to the shared SQLite store by default; add `--backend mcp` to route through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome (repeat --value-metric for nested metrics) agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" --value-metric '{"name":"setup errors","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"count","importance":9,"satisfaction":3}' # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi customer-outcomes get agentic-odi customer-outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete --yes ``` Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server if needed. ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP, REST, Webhook) Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). Every kind implements the same `Connector` protocol and normalizes payloads into `IngestBatch` records. ```bash # MCP: act as an MCP client and pull catalog, resources, and configured tools python -m cli connectors add mcp --name gong --url http://localhost:9000/mcp --tool latest_quote # REST: pull a JSON document and read records from a dot path python -m cli connectors add rest --name jira --url https://jira.example/api/issues --header "Authorization=Bearer $TOKEN" --records-key result.issues # Webhook: POST a configured request to a webhook inbox and ingest its response python -m cli connectors add webhook --name feedback --url https://hooks.example/inbox --method POST python -m cli connectors list python -m cli connectors health --name gong python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong ``` Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and appended to the in-process ingest sink. Pass `--job-id`, `--step-id`, or `--outcome-id` to also map evidence-bearing records into the ODI store, then promote them when they are ready: ```bash python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong --job-id agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi evidence promote --to outcome --job-id --statement "Minimize the time to onboard when signing up" --importance 8 --satisfaction 4 ``` Mapping stays separate from the connector package: connectors emit records, `connectors.mapping` produces evidence drafts, and the CLI writes them to the ODI store. ### ⚡ Living Studio Run Modes The Living Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly. **Architecture** ```text ┌────────────────────────────┐ /api (JSON) ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Living Studio SPA │ ────────────▶ │ local_server (sidecar) │ │ React + TS + Vite │ /api/chat │ FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100 │ │ (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │ - config / health / canvas │ └────────────────────────────┘ SSE stream │ - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │ │ - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop) │ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ │ MCP (HTTP) ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ mcp_server :8000/mcp │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ▲ │ OpenAI-compatible ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐ │ Your local LLM backend │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ``` **1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)** ```bash npm --prefix studio run build # build the SPA into studio/dist python -m client.run # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100 ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | **2. Web — dev with hot reload** (Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar): ```bash npm --prefix studio run dev:full # MCP + sidecar + Vite together # open http://localhost:5173 ``` **3. Desktop — Tauri 2** (the app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself): ```bash npm --prefix studio run tauri dev # dev window npm --prefix studio run tauri build # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows) ``` > [!NOTE] > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu: > > ```bash > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \ > libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64 > ``` > > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`. #### 🔐 Desktop signing & updater secrets Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub Actions secrets. | Secret | Purpose | |---|---| | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. | | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). | | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. | | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. | | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. | | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. | Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via **Settings → Check for updates**. #### 🔑 Managing the updater signing key The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in CI, or attached to a build artifact. 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it: ```bash npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f ``` This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub` (public). 2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`: ```jsonc { "plugins": { "updater": { "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"], "pubkey": "" } } } ``` 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions: ```bash mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/ chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key ``` Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives. Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing installs. 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI: ```bash gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body "" # only if you set a password ``` 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed): ```bash gh secret list ``` 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public key ahead of the cut-over. > [!CAUTION] > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI formulas are unchanged. ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Living Studio sidecar: ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server \ --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ --model_alias local-tools-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ --chat_format openai ``` This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 4. **Point the Living Studio at the local server** The sidecar reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks): | Variable | Default | |---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's **Settings** panel. 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models ``` If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. - Start the MCP server and the Living Studio (via `python -m client.run` or `npm --prefix studio run dev:full`). - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.” - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. ### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. --- ## 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: ```bash # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) uv run --directory core mypy . uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . uv run --directory local_server mypy . uv run --directory client mypy . uv run --directory cli mypy . uv run --directory connectors mypy . # Security scanning uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src # Tests (same as CI) uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` ### 🖥️ Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio) The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally: ```bash npm --prefix studio run lint # ESLint npm --prefix studio run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm --prefix studio test -- --run # Vitest (run once) npm --prefix studio run build # production build → studio/dist cd studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check ``` To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv tool install pre-commit pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: ```bash pre-commit run --all-files ``` --- ## ✅ Testing Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: ```bash uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` ### 📊 Test Coverage Map | File | What it covers | |---|---| | to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. --- ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. To enable: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve` 3. Start Pi: `pi` The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.) > [!NOTE] > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. ### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting - **When editing Python files**, either: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: ```bash uv run ruff format . ``` - **CI behavior**: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. ## 🤖 Superpowers with Freebuff This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for [Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required: - **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool. - **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules, the Freebuff tool mapping, and the mandatory one-worktree-per-task rule at session start. - **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` maps skill actions to Freebuff tools. Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify. See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for update and troubleshooting notes. --- ## Quick Install (Binary) Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install the latest release with one command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer places the binary under `~/.local/share/agentic-odi/versions//`, creates a `current` symlink, and symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. If `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH, add it (e.g., `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`). On Windows, the PowerShell installer uses `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\` and copies `.exe` files to `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\bin\`. ### Update By default, `odi` auto-checks for updates once every 24 hours and applies the update on the next run (auto-update is enabled by default). Control behavior with: - `odi update` — explicit check and update - `--no-update` flag — skip auto-update for this run - `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` — disable auto-update globally When running from a non-frozen source install, auto-update is suppressed automatically. ### Install layout ``` ~/.local/share/agentic-odi/ ├── versions// │ └── odi (and bundled files) └── current -> versions/ ~/.local/bin/ ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi ├── odipm ├── odi-cli └── agentic-odi ~/.config/agentic-odi/ # state/preferences ``` Environment variables: `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR` (override install root), `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_BIN_HOME`. The default backend is `local` (`--backend local`); no MCP server is required. ### Unsigned binaries macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi` (if needed). Windows SmartScreen may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you trust the release. ## ☁️ Deployment The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint Integrate via the MCP protocol at: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** > [!IMPORTANT] > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client. --- ## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps All roadmap milestones below are implemented: - [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests. - [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: `connectors.mapping` turns ingest records into evidence drafts; `connectors ingest --job-id/--step-id/--outcome-id` captures evidence, and `evidence promote` turns a record into a Job or desired Outcome without coupling connector plumbing to the ODI store. - [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST and webhook connectors implement the same `Connector` protocol, with injectable HTTP transports for tests. - [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Pydantic models for Jobs, Steps, Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, and Evidence, plus `core.odi_schema()` / `agentic-odi schema` / `get_odi_schema` for the canonical JSON Schema. - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: `jobs`, `steps`, `outcomes`, `customer-outcomes`, `evidence`, `score`, and `schema` work against the local SQLite store or the MCP backend. - [x] **Context Tooling**: `get_job_map(job_id)`, `evaluate_outcome(statement)`, `get_odi_schema()`, and the Evidence tools replace the dummy `greet` tool. - [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: The FastMCP server and CLI share a read-through SQLite repository (WAL + append-only event log) at `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`. - [x] **Agentic Integration**: The Living Studio and CLI chat connect an OpenAI-compatible LLM to the MCP server, discover tools with `list_tools`, and let the model call them while ideating features. --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Please ensure any change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) before opening a pull request. --- ## 📄 License No license has been specified for this repository yet. **Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.

## Freebuff Tool Mapping

Skills speak in actions, not tool names. On Freebuff they resolve as follows:

| Action skills request | Freebuff equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Invoke or load a skill | `skill` with the skill directory name (for example `{"name": "brainstorming"}`) |

| Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | No subagent tool is exposed. Do not fabricate a dispatch; use `executing-plans` and do the work inline. For a second pair of eyes, use the `requesting-code-review` reviewer prompt as a structured self-review, or ask your human partner to start a fresh session. |
| Enter plan mode | Freebuff has no plan mode. Write designs to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and plans to `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` with `write_file`. |

Freebuff discovers project skills in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and lists each skill's name and description in the system prompt. Load one by name with the `skill` tool; reading a `SKILL.md` with `read_files` is only a fallback if the tool fails.

This CLI exposes no subagent or task-dispatch tool. Use `executing-plans` instead of `subagent-driven-development`, and do independent tasks sequentially instead of `dispatching-parallel-agents`. Never invent `Task`, `subagent`, or similar tool calls.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
<!-- superpowers:freebuff:end -->

"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field


class Direction(str, Enum):
    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"


class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
    RETENTION = "retention"
    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
    OTHER = "other"


def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))


class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")


class Step(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")


class Outcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
    statement: str = Field(
        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
    )
    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
    )
    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
    )


class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
    name: str
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    object_of_control: str
    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
    statement: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
    category: BusinessImpactCategory
    statement: str
    detail: str | None = None
    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


EvidenceItemType = Literal["catalog", "resource", "tool_result", "manual", "note"]


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    """A captured research record linked (optionally) to ODI artifacts."""

    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    source_name: str = Field(..., description="Connector or person that produced the record")
    source_kind: str = Field(..., description="Connector kind, e.g. mcp, rest, webhook, manual")
    item_type: EvidenceItemType = Field(
        "manual", description="Normalized record kind produced by the connector"
    )
    name: str = Field(..., description="Short human-readable label for the record")
    content: str = Field(..., description="Normalized text content of the record")
    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Original record payload")
    job_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job this evidence supports")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job-map Step this evidence supports")
    outcome_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Desired Outcome this evidence supports")


class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
    )
    customer_value: CustomerValue
    business_value: BusinessValue

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

display.text:
"""
run.py — Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.

Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m mcp_server``) and the Living Studio
sidecar (``uvicorn local_server.app:create_app --factory``) concurrently, then
prints the MCP and Studio URLs. Shutting down this script (Ctrl+C) terminates
both processes.

Usage:
    python -m client.run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
import sys
import time

MCP_PORT = 8000
STUDIO_PORT = 8100

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
)
SPA_DIST = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "studio", "dist")
SPA_BUILD_HINT = "Frontend not built — run `npm --prefix studio run build` to serve the Studio UI."


def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0


def build_commands() -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""
    mcp_command = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"]
    sidecar_command = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "uvicorn",
        "local_server.app:create_app",
        "--factory",
        "--host",
        "127.0.0.1",
        "--port",
        str(STUDIO_PORT),
    ]
    return mcp_command, sidecar_command


def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
        print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
        print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
        sys.exit(1)

    mcp_command, _ = build_commands()
    print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen(mcp_command)  # nosec B603


def start_studio() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(STUDIO_PORT):
        print(f"Warning: Port {STUDIO_PORT} is already in use. The sidecar may fail to start.")

    _, sidecar_command = build_commands()
    print(f"Starting Living Studio sidecar on http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT} ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen(sidecar_command)  # nosec B603


def main() -> None:
    server = None
    studio = None

    def shutdown(signum=None, frame=None):
        print("\nShutting down...")
        if studio:
            studio.terminate()
        if server:
            server.terminate()

        try:
            if studio:
                studio.wait(timeout=5)
            if server:
                server.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            if studio:
                studio.kill()
            if server:
                server.kill()

        print("✅ All processes stopped.")
        sys.exit(0)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown)

    try:
        server = start_server()
        # Give the server a moment to bind its port before the sidecar connects
        time.sleep(2)
        studio = start_studio()

        print("\nBoth processes are running.")
        print(f"MCP Server   -> http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp")
        print(f"Living Studio -> http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT}")
        if not os.path.isdir(SPA_DIST):
            print(f"\n⚠️  {SPA_BUILD_HINT}")
        print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop both.\n")

        # Wait for either process to exit unexpectedly
        while True:
            rc_server = server.poll()
            rc_studio = studio.poll()

            if rc_server is not None:
                print(f"\nServer exited unexpectedly (code {rc_server}).")
                break

            if rc_studio is not None:
                print(f"\nStudio sidecar exited unexpectedly (code {rc_studio}).")
                break

            time.sleep(1)

    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"\nError: {e}")
    finally:
        shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Canonical JSON schemas for every ODI entity.

These schemas are the machine-readable contract used by agents, connectors, and
CLI consumers. They are derived from the Pydantic models so there is exactly one
definition of the ODI dataset.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.models import (
    BusinessValue,
    CustomerOutcome,
    CustomerValue,
    Evidence,
    Job,
    Outcome,
    Step,
    ValueMetric,
)

_SCHEMA_MODELS: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] = {
    "Job": Job,
    "Step": Step,
    "Outcome": Outcome,
    "ValueMetric": ValueMetric,
    "CustomerValue": CustomerValue,
    "BusinessValue": BusinessValue,
    "CustomerOutcome": CustomerOutcome,
    "Evidence": Evidence,
}


def odi_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the JSON schema for each ODI entity keyed by model name."""
    return {name: model.model_json_schema() for name, model in _SCHEMA_MODELS.items()}
