1: # GitHub Pages Marketing Site Design
2: 
3: **Date:** 2026-10-18
4: **Status:** Approved (design authority delegated to the session designer; all builder-check questions answered)
5: **Scope:** Single-page customer-facing site in `website/` + GitHub Actions deploy to GitHub Pages
6: 
7: ## Intent & Why
8: 
9: `README.md` is the project's front door, and it reads like an engineering changelog — right for
10: contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
11: worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
12: ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
13: brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.
14: 
15: The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything: **over-promising on an experimental product is the
16: one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
17: no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.
18: 
19: Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
20: lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,
21: and the "CI green" aggregate.
22: 
23: ## Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done
24: 
25: **Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a shared link, a search, or a
26: referral. Skeptical of AI-tool marketing.
27: > When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to know within one screen whether this is a
28: > real, runnable thing grounded in a method I respect, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it
29: > or leave without guilt.
30: 
31: **Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating whether to wire agents to an ODI data source.
32: > When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint and a copy-paste
33: > quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without talking to anyone.
34: 
35: **Tertiary — the sharing PM (internal champion).** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
36: > When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion — credibly and
37: > soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea instead of from my credibility.
38: 
39: ## Messaging Hierarchy
40: 
41: Binding copy contract (tests enforce the marked strings; micro-polish — punctuation-level tweaks —
42: is builder latitude).
43: 
44: | Level | Copy |
45: |---|---|
46: | Eyebrow pill | `Experimental` |
47: | H1 (hero) | **Your roadmap is a guess.** |
48: | Hero sub | An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them. |
49: | Primary CTA | **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run` (local quickstart) |
50: | Secondary CTA | View on GitHub → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi` |
51: | Tertiary link | Hosted demo — requires a free Prefect account → Horizon chat URL |
52: | Footer tagline | Built with outcomes, not guesses. |
53: 
54: **Section 2 — `#problem`, "Opinion is expensive."** Three parallel beats, one line each, each with
55: a short support line:
56: 
57: 1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
58: 2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
59: 3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.
60: 
61: Section closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."
62: 
63: **Section 3 — `#insight`, "Ask for outcomes, not opinions."** Three plain sentences:
64: 1. Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied
65:    they are with it today.
66: 2. The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.
67: 3. Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.
68: 
69: Then: a small CSS/inline-SVG bar visual (Importance vs Satisfaction, gap highlighted, labeled
70: "Illustrative outcome data"), the formula rendered exactly as the code computes it —
71: `Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)` (source of truth:
72: `core/src/core/models.py:27`), and the stat callout: **86%** innovation success rate — *as reported
73: in ODI literature (Strategyn)*. Plain-text attribution only; no link to the in-repo PDF.
74: 
75: **Section 4 — `#how`, "How it works."** Three steps:
76: 1. **Capture** — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI,
77:    connectors, or The Living Studio.
78: 2. **Query** — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or
79:    hosted.
80: 3. **Steer** — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact
81:    Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.
82: 
83: Accompanies: a stylized Studio illustration (real shipped surfaces, marked "Illustrative"), never a
84: fake screenshot.
85: 
86: **Section 5 — `#run`, "Run it in 60 seconds."** Prerequisites line (Python 3.10+, uv), terminal
87: block with copy button:
88: 
89: ```bash
90: git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git
91: cd agentic-odi
92: uv sync --all-packages
93: python -m client.run
94: ```
95: 
96: Endpoint chips with copy buttons: MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp` · Studio `http://localhost:8501`.
97: MCP client config snippet (local only):
98: 
99: ```json
100: {
101:   "mcpServers": {
102:     "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" }
103:   }
104: }
105: ```
106: 
107: Prose note: hosted credentials come from the maintainers — open an issue. Never invent an auth
108: scheme we cannot document.
109: 
110: **Section 6 — `#status`, "Honest status."** `Experimental` badge; **What works today** (MCP server
111: tools for jobs/steps/outcomes/customer outcomes with opportunity scoring; The Living Studio —
112: Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation, Causal Lineage; CLI `outcomes` +
113: `connectors`; MCP ingest connector; hosted test endpoints requiring auth) and **What's next**
114: (curated from the README roadmap at build time: map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts, more
115: connector kinds, ODI schema definition, context tooling, persistence layer, agentic integration).
116: Standing line: "We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does." Closer: "Questions?
117: Open an issue." → Issues link.
118: 
119: **Footer.** Mark + wordmark, tagline, links (GitHub, Issues, Hosted demo), legal line:
120: `© 2026 Agentic ODI maintainers · All rights reserved` + one-line experimental reminder.
121: 
122: **Voice rules:** warm, direct, second person; plain language; no jargon dumps; **no emoji anywhere
123: on the site** (house copy rule from the first-run onboarding spec — README's emoji style stays in
124: README); no superlatives ("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"); English only.
125: 
126: ## Information Architecture / Sitemap
127: 
128: | Route | File | Notes |
129: |---|---|---|
130: | `/` | `website/index.html` | The entire site. One scroll, seven sections. |
131: | `/404.html` | `website/404.html` | On-brand, **self-contained** (inline styles, absolute link home) so it renders at any depth on project Pages. |
132: 
133: - Sticky compact header: mark + wordmark (left), single CTA "Run it in 60 seconds" (right). No nav
134:   links — one page needs no navigation, but the one obvious action must stay reachable.
135: - In-page anchors: `#problem`, `#insight`, `#how`, `#run`, `#status`.
136: - No sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no blog, no docs pages, no search.
137: 
138: ## Visual Direction
139: 
140: **Type.** No webfonts, zero downloads:
141: - `--font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`
142:   (same stack The Living Studio ships, `client/src/client/app.py:36`)
143: - `--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`
144: 
145: | Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
146: |---|---|---|
147: | H1 | `clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem)` | 700, `-0.02em`, lh 1.05 |
148: | H2 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem)` | 700, `-0.015em`, lh 1.15 |

155: overrides. Palette echoes the shipped Studio dark-glass theme (`#0B0D13` / `#131722` / `#F1F5F9`
156: straight from `app.py`). All ratios measured, WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥ 4.5:1):

159: |---|---|---|---|
160: | `--bg` | `#ffffff` | `#0b0d13` | — |
161: | `--surface` | `#f5f5f7` | `#131722` | — |

164: | `--accent` (button fill, white label) | `#0071e3` | `#0071e3` | white on it: 4.70 (both) |
165: | `--accent-text` (link text) | `#0062c4` | `#409cff` | 5.93 bg, 5.44 surface / 6.86 bg, 6.32 surface |
166: | `--accent-hover` | `#0059b8` | `#0059b8` | white on it: 6.73 |

170: Code blocks are dark (`#0b0d13`) in both schemes — a terminal is a terminal (17.7:1 either way).
171: OG card is fixed dark, self-contained.
172: 
173: **Layout & spacing.** Mobile-first; content max-width 1080px, prose max-width 68ch; inline padding
174: `clamp(20px, 5vw, 40px)`; section padding-block `clamp(72px, 12vw, 140px)`; 8px spacing scale as
175: custom properties; radius 12px cards / 999px pills (echoing the Studio's own radii); 1px hairline

178: **Motion.** Restrained, explanatory, never load-bearing:
179: - Hero stagger on load: eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, 12px fade-up, 60ms stagger, 400ms,

212: | 86% stat + "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)" | Session decision (no link to `knowledge/*.pdf`) | honesty test |
213: | Opportunity formula | `core/src/core/models.py:27-29` | formula test |
214: | Headline, subhead, beats, section titles, CTA labels, tagline, OG copy | **Written fresh** — binding in this spec | structural tests |
215: | Mark, favicon, illustrations, OG art | Created per this spec | asset tests |
216: 
217: Rule: README is the source of truth for every command, URL, and status claim. If the page and
218: README disagree, the page is wrong.
219: 
220: ## Technical Approach
221: 
222: Hand-crafted static HTML + one CSS file + ≤100 lines of vanilla JS. **No framework** (no
223: Astro/Next/React): one page with no routing, no state, no data, no components shared across
224: views — a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill, and charges
225: rent on every one of them. Consequence of no framework: deploy is "copy files", the review diff is
226: readable HTML, Lighthouse is high by construction, and there is zero supply chain on the page.
227: 
228: ```
229: website/
230:   index.html            # the site
231:   404.html              # self-contained fallback
232:   assets/
233:     style.css           # tokens + full design system (no external URLs)
234:     main.js             # ≤100 lines: reveal + copy buttons, defer, progressive enhancement
235:     mark.svg  favicon.svg
236:     og.png    favicon.png   # committed, generated (see OG strategy)
237:   tools/
238:     make_og.py          # regenerates og.png + favicon.png (Pillow, pinned)
239:   tests/
240:     test_site.py  test_assets.py  test_make_og.py
241:     test_workflows.py  test_readme_sync.py
242: ```
243: 
244: - **Paths:** every in-page URL is **relative** (`assets/…`, `#anchor`) so the site works under the
245:   project-Pages base `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future custom domain.
246:   `og:url` / `og:image` / `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
247: - Local preview: `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory website` (preview the 404 by opening
248:   `/404.html` directly — `http.server` serves its own 404).
249: - JS is `defer`'d and additive: the page is complete, styled, and readable with JS disabled.
250: - Python tooling lives only in `tools/` + `tests/`, run from the repo root with the workspace venv.
251: 
252: ## OG / Social Strategy
253: 
254: Social previews are the main earned-distribution artifact — one committed raster, no mystery binary.
255: 
256: - `website/assets/og.png`: **1200×630**, fixed dark card — mark + "Agentic ODI" wordmark,
257:   headline "Your roadmap is a guess.", sub "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity
258:   scores — served over MCP.", bottom row `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi` + Experimental badge.
259: - `website/tools/make_og.py`: the committed, runnable generator (stdlib argparse + Pillow). Writes
260:   `og.png` and `favicon.png`; defaults embed the canonical card copy above. Deterministic output —
261:   fixed palette/positions, no timestamps, `compress_level=9`, font via
262:   `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow's embedded Aileron, SIL OFL — no font file in the repo).
263:   Run: `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
264: - **Regenerability is enforced:** `test_make_og.py` renders fresh bytes and asserts they are
265:   pixel-identical to the committed PNGs. Change the script → the test fails until you regenerate.
266:   Change the card copy → defaults in the script are the source.
267: - Meta contract on `index.html`: `og:type=website`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`
268:   ("Your roadmap is a guess. — Agentic ODI"), `og:description`, `og:url` (canonical Pages URL),
269:   `og:image` (absolute PNG URL), `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image,
270:   `rel=canonical`, `theme-color` per color scheme, both favicons. Title tag ≤ 60 chars:
271:   `Agentic ODI — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes`.
272: - og:image is never loaded by the page itself (page weight unaffected).
273: - No OpenGraph on SVG: scrapers (X, LinkedIn, Slack, iMessage) need raster — hence exactly one PNG.
274: 
275: ## Deploy Pipeline
276: 
277: **`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** (deploy only — its contract is tested in `ci.yml` via
278: `test_workflows.py`, so PRs validate it without triggering a deploy):
279: 
280: - `on: push branches [main] paths [website/**, .github/workflows/pages.yml]`, plus
281:   `workflow_dispatch`.
282: - Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`. Concurrency:
283:   `group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Environment: `github-pages` (URL from the
284:   deployment step).
285: - Job `deploy`, steps: checkout@v7 → `./.github/actions/setup` → **run
286:   `uv run pytest website/tests -q` (verify before publish)** → `actions/configure-pages@v6` →
287:   stage the artifact with
288:   `mkdir -p _site && rsync -a --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/ website/ _site/` →
289:   `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5` (`path: _site`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
290:   Only the site publishes — tests and generator never do; `_site/` is CI-only and gitignored.
291: - **Manual gate:** repository Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" must be set **before
292:   this workflow first runs on `main`**, or the deploy job fails. (One-time toggle; flag before
293:   merge.)
294: 
295: **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a `website` job (setup + `uv run pytest website/tests -q`,
296: timeout 10m) and add `website` to `ci-green`'s `needs`. Root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .`
297: already cover `website/**` once root ruff config exists (below).
298: 
299: ## Accessibility & Performance Budget
300: 
301: **Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA):**
302: - Semantic landmarks (`header`/`main`/`footer`), one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, `lang="en"`.
303: - Contrast: measured pairs in the color table — every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in both schemes.
304: - Full keyboard operability; visible focus ring (≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors); copy controls are
305:   real `<button>`s with accessible names; `aria-live` for "Copied".
306: - Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful links (no "click here"); `prefers-reduced-motion`
307:   respected; viewport meta; tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.
308: 
309: **Performance:**
310: - Zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, zero analytics, zero cookies — the page talks only to
311:   its own origin.
312: - Weights (raw, committed): HTML ≤ 60 KB, CSS ≤ 30 KB, JS ≤ 4 KB (≤ 100 non-blank lines), each SVG
313:   ≤ 10 KB, `favicon.png` ≤ 5 KB, total transferred ≤ 150 KB; `og.png` ≤ 300 KB (test-enforced;
314:   expected ~15–40 KB).
315: - Lighthouse ≥ 95 on Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO (mobile emulation,
316:   manual run before merge — CI has no browser).
317: 
318: ## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
319: 
320: - **Not a docs site, not a blog.** No MkDocs/Docusaurus, no nav maze, no search, no sitemap.
321: - **No framework, no build step, no dependencies on the deployed artifact.**
322: - **No claims the repo can't back:** no dates or milestones; no "open source" or license claim
323:   (repo is all-rights-reserved); no maturity language beyond the Experimental framing; no invented
324:   testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmark numbers; no emoji.
325: - **No dead ends:** no CTAs behind auth (hosted is tertiary, labeled); no personal emails, no
326:   invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
327: - **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
328:   endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
329: - **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
330:   "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
331: - **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
332: - **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
333: - **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.
334: 
335: ## Risks & Mitigations
336: 
337: 1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
338:    flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
339: 2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
340: 3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
341: 4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
342:    links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
343: 5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
344:    steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.
345: 
346: ## Resolved Questions (builder-check × session — all settled)
347: 
348: 1. **Primary CTA** → local quickstart ("Run it in 60 seconds"). Verified live: Horizon chat 302s
349:    to `auth.horizon.prefect.io`, hosted MCP returns 401 — a hero CTA that dead-ends anonymous
350:    visitors in auth is malpractice. Hosted is tertiary, labeled "requires a free Prefect account."
351: 2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
352:    Discord.
353: 3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
354:    requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
355: 4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
356:    (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
357: 5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
358:    mirroring the README roadmap.
359: 6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
360:    "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
361: 7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
362:    the copyrighted in-repo PDF.
363: 
364: ## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)
365: 
366: 1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
367:    Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`
368:    (`core/src/core/models.py:28`). The page shows the real formula, and a test pins page ↔ code.
369: 2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):
370:    `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` ships the Aileron font inside Pillow — real typography, no font
371:    binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
372:    Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
373: 3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
374:    lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
375: 4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
376: 5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
377:    assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
378: 6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
379: 7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
380:    `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
381:    YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
382: 8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
383:    gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
384: 9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,
385:    mirroring `cli/pyproject.toml`) so `website/**` Python is linted at repo standards — verified
386:    impact is website-only (no other root-level `.py` files exist).
387: 10. **Hosted link = Horizon chat only**; the `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is never linked
388:     (401) — it is mentioned only as "credentials via an issue."
389: 11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);
390:     no analytics, no sitemap/robots/JSON-LD — SEO comes from meta + structure alone.
391: 12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
392: 13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.
393: 
394: ## What's Left to the Builder
395: 
396: Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
397: details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
398: the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

(End of file - total 398 lines)

# GitHub Pages Marketing Site Design

**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Status:** Approved (design authority delegated to the session designer; all builder-check questions answered)
**Scope:** Single-page customer-facing site in `website/` + GitHub Actions deploy to GitHub Pages

## Intent & Why

`README.md` is the project's front door, and it reads like an engineering changelog — right for
contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.

The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything: **over-promising on an experimental product is the
one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.

Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,
and the "CI green" aggregate.

## Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done

**Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a shared link, a search, or a
referral. Skeptical of AI-tool marketing.
> When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to know within one screen whether this is a
> real, runnable thing grounded in a method I respect, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it
> or leave without guilt.

**Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating whether to wire agents to an ODI data source.
> When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint and a copy-paste
> quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without talking to anyone.

**Tertiary — the sharing PM (internal champion).** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
> When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion — credibly and
> soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea instead of from my credibility.

## Messaging Hierarchy

Binding copy contract (tests enforce the marked strings; micro-polish — punctuation-level tweaks —
is builder latitude).

| Level | Copy |
|---|---|
| Eyebrow pill | `Experimental` |
| H1 (hero) | **Your roadmap is a guess.** |
| Hero sub | An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them. |
| Primary CTA | **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run` (local quickstart) |
| Secondary CTA | View on GitHub → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi` |
| Tertiary link | Hosted demo — requires a free Prefect account → Horizon chat URL |
| Footer tagline | Built with outcomes, not guesses. |

**Section 2 — `#problem`, "Opinion is expensive."** Three parallel beats, one line each, each with
a short support line:

1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.

Section closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."

**Section 3 — `#insight`, "Ask for outcomes, not opinions."** Three plain sentences:
1. Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied
   they are with it today.
2. The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.
3. Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.

Then: a small CSS/inline-SVG bar visual (Importance vs Satisfaction, gap highlighted, labeled
"Illustrative outcome data"), the formula rendered exactly as the code computes it —
`Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)` (source of truth:
`core/src/core/models.py:27`), and the stat callout: **86%** innovation success rate — *as reported
in ODI literature (Strategyn)*. Plain-text attribution only; no link to the in-repo PDF.

**Section 4 — `#how`, "How it works."** Three steps:
1. **Capture** — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI,
   connectors, or The Living Studio.
2. **Query** — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or
   hosted.
3. **Steer** — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact
   Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.

Accompanies: a stylized Studio illustration (real shipped surfaces, marked "Illustrative"), never a
fake screenshot.

**Section 5 — `#run`, "Run it in 60 seconds."** Prerequisites line (Python 3.10+, uv), terminal
block with copy button:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git
cd agentic-odi
uv sync --all-packages
python -m client.run
```

Endpoint chips with copy buttons: MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp` · Studio `http://localhost:8501`.
MCP client config snippet (local only):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" }
  }
}
```

Prose note: hosted credentials come from the maintainers — open an issue. Never invent an auth
scheme we cannot document.

**Section 6 — `#status`, "Honest status."** `Experimental` badge; **What works today** (MCP server
tools for jobs/steps/outcomes/customer outcomes with opportunity scoring; The Living Studio —
Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation, Causal Lineage; CLI `outcomes` +
`connectors`; MCP ingest connector; hosted test endpoints requiring auth) and **What's next**
(curated from the README roadmap at build time: map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts, more
connector kinds, ODI schema definition, context tooling, persistence layer, agentic integration).
Standing line: "We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does." Closer: "Questions?
Open an issue." → Issues link.

**Footer.** Mark + wordmark, tagline, links (GitHub, Issues, Hosted demo), legal line:
`© 2026 Agentic ODI maintainers · All rights reserved` + one-line experimental reminder.

**Voice rules:** warm, direct, second person; plain language; no jargon dumps; **no emoji anywhere
on the site** (house copy rule from the first-run onboarding spec — README's emoji style stays in
README); no superlatives ("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"); English only.

## Information Architecture / Sitemap

| Route | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `website/index.html` | The entire site. One scroll, seven sections. |
| `/404.html` | `website/404.html` | On-brand, **self-contained** (inline styles, absolute link home) so it renders at any depth on project Pages. |

- Sticky compact header: mark + wordmark (left), single CTA "Run it in 60 seconds" (right). No nav
  links — one page needs no navigation, but the one obvious action must stay reachable.
- In-page anchors: `#problem`, `#insight`, `#how`, `#run`, `#status`.
- No sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no blog, no docs pages, no search.

## Visual Direction

**Type.** No webfonts, zero downloads:
- `--font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`
  (same stack The Living Studio ships, `client/src/client/app.py:36`)
- `--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`

| Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | `clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem)` | 700, `-0.02em`, lh 1.05 |
| H2 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem)` | 700, `-0.015em`, lh 1.15 |
| H3 / beats | `1.25rem` | 600, lh 1.3 |
| Body / lead | `1.0625rem` (17px) / `1.1875rem` | 400, lh 1.6 |
| Eyebrow, badges | `0.75rem` | 600, `0.08em`, uppercase |
| Code | `0.9375rem` mono | lh 1.55 |

**Color.** Tokens as CSS custom properties; `:root` = light, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
overrides. Palette echoes the shipped Studio dark-glass theme (`#0B0D13` / `#131722` / `#F1F5F9`
straight from `app.py`). All ratios measured, WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥ 4.5:1):

| Token | Light | Dark | Contrast (light / dark) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#ffffff` | `#0b0d13` | — |
| `--surface` | `#f5f5f7` | `#131722` | — |
| `--text` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f1f5f9` | 16.8 on bg / 17.7 on bg |
| `--muted` | `#6e6e73` | `#94a3b8` | 5.07 bg, 4.66 surface / 7.58 bg, 6.98 surface |
| `--accent` (button fill, white label) | `#0071e3` | `#0071e3` | white on it: 4.70 (both) |
| `--accent-text` (link text) | `#0062c4` | `#409cff` | 5.93 bg, 5.44 surface / 6.86 bg, 6.32 surface |
| `--accent-hover` | `#0059b8` | `#0059b8` | white on it: 6.73 |
| `--badge` (fg on bg) | `#475569` on `#e2e8f0` | `#cbd5e1` on `#1e293b` | 6.15 / 9.85 |
| `--border` | `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` | `rgba(148,163,184,.16)` | decorative only |

Code blocks are dark (`#0b0d13`) in both schemes — a terminal is a terminal (17.7:1 either way).
OG card is fixed dark, self-contained.

**Layout & spacing.** Mobile-first; content max-width 1080px, prose max-width 68ch; inline padding
`clamp(20px, 5vw, 40px)`; section padding-block `clamp(72px, 12vw, 140px)`; 8px spacing scale as
custom properties; radius 12px cards / 999px pills (echoing the Studio's own radii); 1px hairline
borders. Beats and steps go two-column at ≥720px.

**Motion.** Restrained, explanatory, never load-bearing:
- Hero stagger on load: eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, 12px fade-up, 60ms stagger, 400ms,
  `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` — pure CSS, no JS.
- Scroll reveal: sections fade-up once when 15% visible (IntersectionObserver). Default state is
  **visible**; JS opts content into the hidden-then-reveal state only after it loads, so no-JS
  readers never see hidden content.
- Buttons: 150ms `background-color`/`transform`, hover `translateY(-1px)`, active `scale(.98)`.
- Copy button swaps its label to "Copied" for 1.5s, announced via an `aria-live="polite"` span.
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: all transforms/stagger removed, reveals off, content
  immediate.

**Imagery & assets (none exist in the repo — all created):**
- **Mark** (`mark.svg`, hand-authored, viewBox `0 0 32 32`): rounded-square canvas with an
  ascending two-step polyline and a filled dot at the apex — the opportunity curve breaking
  upward. Accent stroke `#0071e3`, hairline frame. Works at 16px, single color-safe.
- **Favicon:** `favicon.svg` (same geometry) + `favicon.png` 32×32 (generated, dark tile, for
  browsers that ignore SVG icons).
- **Opportunity visual:** pure CSS/inline SVG bars in `#insight`, `aria`-labeled, marked
  "Illustrative outcome data".
- **Studio illustration:** stylized abstraction of shipped surfaces only (Opportunity Landscape,
  Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation — verified in `client/src/client/app.py:683-838`), marked
  "Illustrative". Depicting vaporware on a page whose thesis is "no guesses" would self-destruct.
- All decorative SVGs `aria-hidden="true"`; no stock photos, no icon fonts, no emoji.

## Content Sources

| Content | Source | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Quickstart commands (`uv sync --all-packages`, `python -m client.run`) | README §Getting Started — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Local endpoints (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`, `http://localhost:8501`) | README One-Command Launch — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Hosted chat URL | README §Deployment — **verbatim**; the label "requires a free Prefect account" is fresh | `test_readme_sync.py` + allowlist |
| Experimental framing, maturity claims | README banner — adapted, no new claims | review + honesty tests |
| What works today / What's next | README roadmap checkboxes, curated at build time (re-read README in Task 2 of the plan) | review focus |
| License/legal line | README §License — adapted ("All rights reserved") | honesty test |
| 86% stat + "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)" | Session decision (no link to `knowledge/*.pdf`) | honesty test |
| Opportunity formula | `core/src/core/models.py:27-29` | formula test |
| Headline, subhead, beats, section titles, CTA labels, tagline, OG copy | **Written fresh** — binding in this spec | structural tests |
| Mark, favicon, illustrations, OG art | Created per this spec | asset tests |

Rule: README is the source of truth for every command, URL, and status claim. If the page and
README disagree, the page is wrong.

## Technical Approach

Hand-crafted static HTML + one CSS file + ≤100 lines of vanilla JS. **No framework** (no
Astro/Next/React): one page with no routing, no state, no data, no components shared across
views — a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill, and charges
rent on every one of them. Consequence of no framework: deploy is "copy files", the review diff is
readable HTML, Lighthouse is high by construction, and there is zero supply chain on the page.

```
website/
  index.html            # the site
  404.html              # self-contained fallback
  assets/
    style.css           # tokens + full design system (no external URLs)
    main.js             # ≤100 lines: reveal + copy buttons, defer, progressive enhancement
    mark.svg  favicon.svg
    og.png    favicon.png   # committed, generated (see OG strategy)
  tools/
    make_og.py          # regenerates og.png + favicon.png (Pillow, pinned)
  tests/
    test_site.py  test_assets.py  test_make_og.py
    test_workflows.py  test_readme_sync.py
```

- **Paths:** every in-page URL is **relative** (`assets/…`, `#anchor`) so the site works under the
  project-Pages base `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future custom domain.
  `og:url` / `og:image` / `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
- Local preview: `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory website` (preview the 404 by opening
  `/404.html` directly — `http.server` serves its own 404).
- JS is `defer`'d and additive: the page is complete, styled, and readable with JS disabled.
- Python tooling lives only in `tools/` + `tests/`, run from the repo root with the workspace venv.

## OG / Social Strategy

Social previews are the main earned-distribution artifact — one committed raster, no mystery binary.

- `website/assets/og.png`: **1200×630**, fixed dark card — mark + "Agentic ODI" wordmark,
  headline "Your roadmap is a guess.", sub "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity
  scores — served over MCP.", bottom row `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi` + Experimental badge.
- `website/tools/make_og.py`: the committed, runnable generator (stdlib argparse + Pillow). Writes
  `og.png` and `favicon.png`; defaults embed the canonical card copy above. Deterministic output —
  fixed palette/positions, no timestamps, `compress_level=9`, font via
  `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow's embedded Aileron, SIL OFL — no font file in the repo).
  Run: `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
- **Regenerability is enforced:** `test_make_og.py` renders fresh bytes and asserts they are
  pixel-identical to the committed PNGs. Change the script → the test fails until you regenerate.
  Change the card copy → defaults in the script are the source.
- Meta contract on `index.html`: `og:type=website`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`
  ("Your roadmap is a guess. — Agentic ODI"), `og:description`, `og:url` (canonical Pages URL),
  `og:image` (absolute PNG URL), `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image,
  `rel=canonical`, `theme-color` per color scheme, both favicons. Title tag ≤ 60 chars:
  `Agentic ODI — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes`.
- og:image is never loaded by the page itself (page weight unaffected).
- No OpenGraph on SVG: scrapers (X, LinkedIn, Slack, iMessage) need raster — hence exactly one PNG.

## Deploy Pipeline

**`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** (deploy only — its contract is tested in `ci.yml` via
`test_workflows.py`, so PRs validate it without triggering a deploy):

- `on: push branches [main] paths [website/**, .github/workflows/pages.yml]`, plus
  `workflow_dispatch`.
- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`. Concurrency:
  `group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Environment: `github-pages` (URL from the
  deployment step).
- Job `deploy`, steps: checkout@v7 → `./.github/actions/setup` → **run
  `uv run pytest website/tests -q` (verify before publish)** → `actions/configure-pages@v6` →
  stage the artifact with
  `mkdir -p _site && rsync -a --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/ website/ _site/` →
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5` (`path: _site`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
  Only the site publishes — tests and generator never do; `_site/` is CI-only and gitignored.
- **Manual gate:** repository Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" must be set **before
  this workflow first runs on `main`**, or the deploy job fails. (One-time toggle; flag before
  merge.)

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a `website` job (setup + `uv run pytest website/tests -q`,
timeout 10m) and add `website` to `ci-green`'s `needs`. Root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .`
already cover `website/**` once root ruff config exists (below).

## Accessibility & Performance Budget

**Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA):**
- Semantic landmarks (`header`/`main`/`footer`), one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, `lang="en"`.
- Contrast: measured pairs in the color table — every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in both schemes.
- Full keyboard operability; visible focus ring (≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors); copy controls are
  real `<button>`s with accessible names; `aria-live` for "Copied".
- Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful links (no "click here"); `prefers-reduced-motion`
  respected; viewport meta; tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.

**Performance:**
- Zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, zero analytics, zero cookies — the page talks only to
  its own origin.
- Weights (raw, committed): HTML ≤ 60 KB, CSS ≤ 30 KB, JS ≤ 4 KB (≤ 100 non-blank lines), each SVG
  ≤ 10 KB, `favicon.png` ≤ 5 KB, total transferred ≤ 150 KB; `og.png` ≤ 300 KB (test-enforced;
  expected ~15–40 KB).
- Lighthouse ≥ 95 on Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO (mobile emulation,
  manual run before merge — CI has no browser).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- **Not a docs site, not a blog.** No MkDocs/Docusaurus, no nav maze, no search, no sitemap.
- **No framework, no build step, no dependencies on the deployed artifact.**
- **No claims the repo can't back:** no dates or milestones; no "open source" or license claim
  (repo is all-rights-reserved); no maturity language beyond the Experimental framing; no invented
  testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmark numbers; no emoji.
- **No dead ends:** no CTAs behind auth (hosted is tertiary, labeled); no personal emails, no
  invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
- **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
  endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
- **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
  "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
- **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
- **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
- **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.

## Risks & Mitigations

1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
   flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
   links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
   steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.

## Resolved Questions (builder-check × session — all settled)

1. **Primary CTA** → local quickstart ("Run it in 60 seconds"). Verified live: Horizon chat 302s
   to `auth.horizon.prefect.io`, hosted MCP returns 401 — a hero CTA that dead-ends anonymous
   visitors in auth is malpractice. Hosted is tertiary, labeled "requires a free Prefect account."
2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
   Discord.
3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
   requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
   (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
   mirroring the README roadmap.
6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
   "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
   the copyrighted in-repo PDF.

## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)

1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
   Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`
   (`core/src/core/models.py:28`). The page shows the real formula, and a test pins page ↔ code.
2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):
   `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` ships the Aileron font inside Pillow — real typography, no font
   binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
   Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
   lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
   assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
   `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
   YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
   gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,
   mirroring `cli/pyproject.toml`) so `website/**` Python is linted at repo standards — verified
   impact is website-only (no other root-level `.py` files exist).
10. **Hosted link = Horizon chat only**; the `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is never linked
    (401) — it is mentioned only as "credentials via an issue."
11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);
    no analytics, no sitemap/robots/JSON-LD — SEO comes from meta + structure alone.
12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.

## What's Left to the Builder

Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

<content>
1: # First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design
2: 
3: **Date:** 2026-10-16
4: **Status:** Approved
5: **Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile
6: 
7: ## Intent & Why
8: 
9: Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.
10: 
11: Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.
12: 
13: ## Goals
14: 
15: - First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
16: - Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
17: - Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
18: - Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
19: - `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
20: - PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).
21: 
22: ## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
23: 
24: - No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
25: - No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
26: - No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
27: - No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
28: - No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).
29: 
30: ## User Flow
31: 
32: ### 1. Trigger
33: 
34: - Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
35: - Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
36: - Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.
37: 
38: ### 2. Opening (the designed moment)
39: 
40: ```
41: Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.
42: 
43: Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
44: First: what product are you working on?
45: Paste a product URL or company name:
46: ```
47: 
48: ### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect
49: 
50: 1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
51: 2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
52: 3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
53: 4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
54: 5. Show the confirmation card:
55: 
56: ```
57: Based on sentry.io — does this look right?
58: 
59:   Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
60:   Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
61:   Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
62:   Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging
63: 
64:   [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
65: ```
66: 
67: 6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).
68: 
69: ### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)
70: 
71: Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):
72: 
73: 1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
74: 2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
75: 3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).
76: 
77: Then the same confirmation card and save.
78: 
79: ### 5. After onboarding
80: 
81: - Baseline file presence suppresses the hook forever.
82: - `odi setup` — full re-run, overwrites file (keeps a timestamped backup).
83: - `odi profile` — print the current card from the file. (`setup`/`profile` confirmed: plain language, matches the reserved `odi` alias.)
84: - All user-facing copy (hints, "Try: …" lines) uses the invoked program name (`sys.argv[0]` basename) so it is valid on any install, `odi` or `agentic-odi`.
85: - Skills/agent consumption (future): the file path is stable and documented; `odi profile --json` dumps machine-readable baseline.
86: 
87: ## Data Model
88: 
89: `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):
90: 
91: ```json
92: {
93:   "schema_version": 1,
94:   "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
95:   "source": "url" | "typed",
96:   "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
97:   "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
98:   "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
99:   "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
100:   "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
101:   "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
102:   "confidence": "high" | "low"
103: }
104: ```
105: 
106: Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.
107: 
108: ## Code Layout (new)
109: 
110: ```
111: cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
112: cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
113: cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
114: cli/tests/test_onboard.py
115: cli/tests/test_infer.py
116: cli/tests/test_profile.py
117: ```
118: 
119: - `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
120: - httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.
121: 
122: ## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)
123: 
124: - Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
125: - Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
126: - Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
127: - Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
128: - `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.
129: 
130: ## Constraints
131: 
132: - Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
133: - Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.
134: 
135: ## Review Focus (likely to bite)
136: 
137: 1. Fetch hang/timeout on weird sites — hard 8s timeout, errors → typed path.
138: 2. TTY detection wrong in some terminals — conservative check; hint-line behavior in non-TTY.
139: 3. Inference confidently wrong — confirmation card always shown; nothing saved without confirm.
140: 4. Concurrent first runs — file written atomically (temp file + replace).
141: 5. `--version` and help must never trigger onboarding.
142: 
143: ## Resolved Questions
144: 
145: 1. Command naming: **`odi setup` / `odi profile`** (plain language; matches reserved `odi` alias). Copy uses the invoked program name.
146: 2. `current_focus`: **just-in-time only** — not asked on the happy path; asked as the 3rd typed question in the fallback path.
147: 
148: ## Builder Calls (made during review)
149: 
150: 1. Typed-path fields: schema fields other than `schema_version` are nullable; card renders only non-null lines.
151: 2. `httpx` added as an explicit `cli` package dependency (spec previously, incorrectly, claimed it already was).

(End of file - total 151 lines)
</content>

- No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
- No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
- No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).

## User Flow

### 1. Trigger

- Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
- Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
- Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.

### 2. Opening (the designed moment)

```
Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.

Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
First: what product are you working on?
Paste a product URL or company name:
```

### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect

1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
5. Show the confirmation card:

```
Based on sentry.io — does this look right?

  Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
  Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
  Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
  Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging

  [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
```

6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).

### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)

Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):

1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).

Then the same confirmation card and save.

### 5. After onboarding

- Baseline file presence suppresses the hook forever.
- `odi setup` — full re-run, overwrites file (keeps a timestamped backup).
- `odi profile` — print the current card from the file. (`setup`/`profile` confirmed: plain language, matches the reserved `odi` alias.)
- All user-facing copy (hints, "Try: …" lines) uses the invoked program name (`sys.argv[0]` basename) so it is valid on any install, `odi` or `agentic-odi`.
- Skills/agent consumption (future): the file path is stable and documented; `odi profile --json` dumps machine-readable baseline.

## Data Model

`~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "source": "url" | "typed",
  "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
  "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
  "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
  "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
  "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
  "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
  "confidence": "high" | "low"
}
```

Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.

## Code Layout (new)

```
cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
cli/tests/test_onboard.py
cli/tests/test_infer.py
cli/tests/test_profile.py
```

- `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
- httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.

## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)

- Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
- Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
- Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
- Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
- `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.

## Constraints

- Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
- Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.

## Review Focus (likely to bite)

1. Fetch hang/timeout on weird sites — hard 8s timeout, errors → typed path.
2. TTY detection wrong in some terminals — conservative check; hint-line behavior in non-TTY.
3. Inference confidently wrong — confirmation card always shown; nothing saved without confirm.
4. Concurrent first runs — file written atomically (temp file + replace).
5. `--version` and help must never trigger onboarding.

## Resolved Questions

1. Command naming: **`odi setup` / `odi profile`** (plain language; matches reserved `odi` alias). Copy uses the invoked program name.
2. `current_focus`: **just-in-time only** — not asked on the happy path; asked as the 3rd typed question in the fallback path.

## Builder Calls (made during review)

1. Typed-path fields: schema fields other than `schema_version` are nullable; card renders only non-null lines.
2. `httpx` added as an explicit `cli` package dependency (spec previously, incorrectly, claimed it already was).

1: # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
2: 
3: This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
4: 
5: > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
10: 
11: This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
12: 
13: ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
14: 
15: ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
16: 
17: ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
22: 
23: - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
24: - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
25: - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
26: - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
31: 
32: - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
33: - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
34: - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
35: 
36:   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
37: 
38:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
39:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
40:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
41:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
42: 
43: - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
48: 
49: - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
50:   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
51:   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
52:   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
53:   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
54:   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
55:   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
56:   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
57:   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
58: 
59: - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
60: - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
65: 
66: - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
67:   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
68:   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
69: 
70: - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
71: 
72:   ```
73:   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
74:   ```
75: 
76: - **Interpretation**:
77:   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
78:   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
79:   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
80: 
81: - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
86: 
87: - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
88: - Segments can be:
89:   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
90:   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
91:   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
92: 
93: - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
98: 
99: Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
100: 
101: | Strategy | When to use |
102: |---|---|
103: | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
104: | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
105: | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
106: 
107: - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
112: 
113: These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
114: 
115: | DO | DON'T |
116: |---|---|
117: | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
118: | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
119: | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
120: | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
121: | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
122: | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
123: | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
128: - **Language**: Python 3.10+
129: - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
130: - **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
131: - **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
132: - **UI / Chat Client**: `streamlit`
133: - **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
134: - **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
135: - **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 🌳 Git Worktree Workflow (Mandatory)
140: 
141: Each separate task gets its own git worktree and branch. This keeps in-flight work from colliding — for example, two features editing `cli/` at once — and keeps the primary checkout clean.
142: 
143: ### Rules
144: 
145: - ✅ **Create a worktree before starting a task**: `git worktree add .worktrees/<task> -b <type>/<task>`, then do all of the work there.
146: - ✅ **Use the project worktree directory**: `.worktrees/` at the repo root (already git-ignored). Branch prefixes: `feature/`, `fix/`, `topic/`.
147: - ✅ **Load the `using-git-worktrees` skill** when starting isolated work; follow its Step 0 isolation check before creating anything.
148: - ✅ **One task per worktree**: a rebase, a bug fix, a review, and a feature are separate tasks and therefore separate worktrees.
149: - ❌ **Never start a new task in a checkout that already holds another task's branch or uncommitted work.** If you find yourself doing so, stop, create a worktree, and move the work there before continuing.
150: - ✅ **Remove the worktree** (`git worktree remove .worktrees/<task>`) once the branch is merged or abandoned.
151: 
152: ---
153: 
154: ## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail
155: 
156: `README.md` is the **primary human-facing source of truth** for this project. The agent MUST keep it current at all times.
157: 
158: ### When to update README.md
159: 
160: Update `README.md` whenever any of the following change:
161: 
162: | Change type | README section to update |
163: |---|---|
164: | New or removed Python file | **Code Overview** |
165: | New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | **Prerequisites** |
166: | New way to run the project | **Running the Environment** |
167: | New MCP tool or capability | **Code Overview** / relevant section |
168: | New workflow or agent instruction | **Getting Started → Agent-driven testing** |
169: | Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | **Deployment** |
170: | Roadmap item completed or added | **Roadmap & Next Steps** |
171: 
172: ### Rules
173: 
174: - ✅ **Update README in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
175: - ✅ **Keep the "Running the Environment" section accurate**: always reflect `python -m client.run` as the recommended launch command.
176: - ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
177: - ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
178: - ❌ **Never leave README in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
183: 
184: ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
185: - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
186: - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
187:   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
188:   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
189: - **Tool Creation**: 
190:   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
191:   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
192:   - **Capability Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update the `get_capabilities` tool's human-readable return string to ensure the capability set exactly matches the code.
193: 
194: ### 2. Async / Client Practices
195: - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
196: - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
197: 
198: ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
199: - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
200: - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
201: 
202: ### 4. General Philosophy
203: - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
204: - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
205: - **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `connectors/` workspace package. New kinds implement `connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
206: - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
207: 
208: ### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
209: - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
210: - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
211: - **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
212: - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
213: - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
214: - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
215: - **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

(End of file - total 215 lines)
</content>
